text:
Martin Fehérváry has never been a scorer, and this season has made the point loudly: no goals, 4 assists and only 9 shots in 21 games. What he does is defend. He's playing about 21 minutes a night, has blocked 54 shots, and at five on five the Capitals have taken 54% of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) with him on, even though the raw shot attempts lean the other way. He also skates in the 95th percentile for top speed, a real asset for a defensive defenseman.

Washington's results haven't matched that work. The Capitals have scored 12.2 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points during a rough November for the team. That kind of gap usually swings back. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 94th percentile among defensemen for primary shot assists last season, so there's more passing in his game than this line shows. Our numbers project about 23 points. Watch his ice time, down to about 19:40 a night over his last ten games.
headline: Martin Fehérváry defends well, and nothing goes in
